_note: The source registry (docs/data-sources.md section 4): one entry per outside source, with its cadence, hosts, whether a key is needed, the dated robots.txt and terms checks, the verdict under the watcher rule (docs/county-data-build-vs-buy.md 3.4) and the principal's decision. This first set is the county foreclosure-notice watchers, from the recon of 2026-11-18 (docs/county-watchers-recon.md). A rule file: sources only, NO prospect data, NO borrower, lender or person names. verdict is allowed, not_allowed or unclear; only an allowed source may be enabled, and enabled means cleared to build and run, not that an adapter exists. fields says where each field of a notice appears: list (on the list page itself), document (only on the linked notice), absent, or not_seen (the source could not be read). Requests send the User-Agent in config.json (fdic.userAgent) and stay at or under 3 a minute per host, or slower where robots.txt sets a Crawl-delay. A terms check older than a year, a new challenge page, a block or a cease-and-desist letter stops the source until a principal decides.

sources.name: Caldwell County Clerk: posted notices of trustee's sale
sources.format: HTML list (li.doc-item, one per notice, grouped under sale-month headings, ?year=YYYY filter, GET search ?q=); one PDF per notice, a scanned image (200 dpi grayscale) with an OCR text layer
sources.history: Sale dates from 2020 to date (610 notices on 2026-11-18)

terms.automatedAccess: not forbidden; unreasonable load and circumventing rate limits are
terms.quote: You may read, print and download material from this site for personal, non-commercial use, and for any use permitted by the Texas Public Information Act. You may not: ... use automated means to place an unreasonable load on the site, or to circumvent its rate limits; harvest personal information from the site for solicitation
terms.version: effective 21 August 2026; the page says it is under review by the County District Attorney's office

sources.verdictBasis: An official list the law requires to be public; robots.txt allows the list and the files; the terms allow PIA-permitted use and forbid only unreasonable load; no login, CAPTCHA or challenge.
conditions: One list request a week (twice a week if a principal wants more warning) plus only the PDFs that are new, 21 seconds apart.

Borrower names and any individual named in a notice are never used for outreach, never leave principal context, and are not harvested for solicitation; the signal is the enforcing lender, an institution.
Recheck the disclaimer monthly while the District Attorney's review is open.

principalDecision.use: Lender-level use only, as a use permitted by the Texas Public Information Act; never harvesting personal information for solicitation.
conditions: Lender-level use only: the signal is the enforcing lender, an institution.
No borrower, and no individual named in a notice, is ever contacted from this data.
Recheck the county's disclaimer monthly, because it is under review by the County District Attorney's office.

sources.name: Denver Public Trustee: foreclosure search (GTS)
sources.format: ASP.NET WebForms search app: an empty form on GET; results only by POST with __VIEWSTATE and __EVENTVALIDATION, session cookies, and a hidden g-recaptcha-response field. Its reports page (/foreclosuresearch/reports) lists no report types.
sources.history: GTS software since May 1, 2026; older history not seen

relevant: 7,716 Disallow lines, all for named content pages; none matches /foreclosuresearch/

terms.automatedAccess: not addressed; disclaimers of accuracy and of linked sites only
terms.quote: neither the city nor any of its employees assumes any legal liability or responsibility for the accuracy, completeness or usefulness of any information disclosed

barriers: a reCAPTCHA response field on the search form
sources.verdictBasis: robots.txt and the terms allow it, but results need a form POST and the form carries a reCAPTCHA field, so a watcher could meet a CAPTCHA. The search filters by foreclosure number, borrower or owner name, address, subdivision, status, NED recording date, sold date and scheduled sale date; the result columns were not seen.
toConfirm: Ask the Public Trustee whether automated searching is acceptable and whether the reCAPTCHA is enforced, or whether it will publish a weekly new-foreclosure (NED) report on its GTS reports page, as Jefferson and Douglas do.
